items.label: Iran conflict sharply escalates -- IRGC fires missiles at two US Navy warships, CENTCOM sinks/disables three Iranian tankers
items.detail: On Sept 5, 2026, the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships (a carrier and a guided-missile destroyer, both evaded); CENTCOM retaliated by sinking the crude tanker M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman and disabling M/T Downy and M/T Stark 1 near Kharg Island/Jask, with CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper warning of 'an even higher economic cost' for further Iranian strikes (source: ABC News, Al Jazeera, Yahoo News, all Sept 5, 2026). On Sept 3, Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Brent crude broke above $96/bbl same day (CNBC, Sept 3, 2026); Strait of Hormuz traffic degraded further to 4 vessels transiting Thursday Sept 3 vs. a 10-day average of 15 (The National, Sept 4, 2026). This is a direct US-Iran military exchange, a materially higher-risk escalation than the prior blockade-only phase, and Trump has separately warned of 'the biggest attack of them all... waiting in the wings' (per ABC/Britannica compilation). US equities saw a tech-led selloff on Sept 5 (S&P -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29%, VIX +1.47%, source: Vittarthi Markets, Sept 5, 2026). The account holds no direct oil & gas exposure (CCJ is a uranium miner, not oil & gas) but is 69.54% concentrated in SPY5+SPYL, which would be hit hard by any broad equity selloff or oil-driven inflation surprise.
items.recommendation: Do not add to SPY5/SPYL or initiate new discretionary equity purchases until the direct US-Iran military exchange stabilizes. Accelerate the DBC and TLT diversification actions in this report -- both would partially cushion an oil/inflation-driven equity shock -- rather than waiting for the next scheduled review.

items.label: September 16 FOMC decision -- hike odds diverging further, Sept 11 CPI now the explicit swing catalyst
items.detail: Hike-odds readings have diverged further this week: Forbes cited CME FedWatch at 66% (Aug 31), Yahoo Finance cited ~70.2% (~Sept 5), while Bloomberg and RealEstateNews describe the odds as still near '50-50' pending the Sept 11 CPI print (both Sept 4, 2026).
